topics.title: Geckos: no suction cups, no glue
topics.myth: Geckos stick with suction cups or sticky glue.
topics.truth: Millions of microscopic setae split into billions of tips; van der Waals forces hold them dry.
topics.line: A gecko uses no glue and no suction: billions of tiny hairs touch the wall so closely that molecules hold on.

sources.cite: Autumn et al. 2002, PNAS 99:12252-12256

topics.title: Mosquitoes follow your skin's smell, not sweet blood
topics.myth: Mosquitoes pick people with sweet blood or a certain blood group.
topics.truth: People who attract Aedes aegypti most carry more carboxylic acids on their skin; the preference held for years.
topics.line: Mosquitoes aren't choosing your blood; they're following the smell your skin makes.
topics.human_scale: An invisible scent trail around one person and not the next.

sources.cite: De Obaldia et al. 2022, Cell 185:4099-4116

topics.title: A woodpecker's skull is NOT a shock absorber
topics.myth: Woodpeckers have shock-absorbing skulls that cushion every hit.
topics.truth: High-speed video and models show the head acts as a stiff hammer; absorbing shock would weaken the peck, and the small brain stays below concussion loads.
topics.line: A woodpecker's head isn't a cushion; it's a stiff hammer, and its tiny brain is why it's safe.
topics.human_scale: A hammer with a soft head would barely drive a nail.

sources.cite: Van Wassenbergh et al. 2022, Current Biology 32:3189-3194

topics.title: Popcorn jumps on a starch leg
topics.myth: Popcorn jumps because it explodes like a tiny bomb.
topics.truth: Near 180 °C the hull breaks; a starch 'leg' pushes on the pan and launches the kernel, and the pop is water vapour escaping.
topics.line: Popcorn doesn't jump from the bang; a leg of hot starch kicks the pan and launches it.

sources.cite: Virot & Ponomarenko 2015, J R Soc Interface 12:20141247

topics.title: Chilli isn't hot: it switches on your heat sensor
topics.myth: Chilli makes your mouth physically hotter.
topics.truth: Capsaicin opens TRPV1, the ion channel that also fires for dangerous heat above ~43 °C; the brain reads it as burning.
topics.line: Chilli doesn't heat your mouth; it switches on the same sensor that warns you about dangerous heat.
topics.human_scale: Like pressing a fire alarm without starting a fire.

sources.cite: Caterina et al. 1997, Nature 389:816-824

topics.title: Why water dances on a very hot pan
topics.myth: A hotter pan always boils a drop away faster.
topics.truth: Above the Leidenfrost point a vapour cushion lifts and insulates the drop, so it lasts longer and skates.
topics.line: On a hot enough pan, water lasts longer: it floats on a cushion of its own steam.
topics.human_scale: An air-hockey puck, but the air is steam.

sources.cite: Quéré 2013, Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics 45:197-215
